speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings. To understand what might be causing this, have you noticed any discharge, fever, or dizziness since the surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Frey's Syndrome (Gustatory Sweating).

Based on your history of ear surgery and the specific complaint of "shooting pain when eating," this is a classic presentation of nerve regeneration where facial nerves grow into sweat glands near the ear. The pain triggered by chewing and the difficulty with earrings (due to skin sensitivity/sweating) confirm this condition.
